title: CHEAP RACECAR BATTLE Damage Report & Budget Updates
coverage: full transcript read (0:00-38:08); 0:00-1:21 is a sponsor read, 2:42-4:46 merch talk

context.edition: CRC 1 ($7,500) - post Sick Week ('Drag and Drive on Sick Week') budget audit + teardown
context.edition_note: The same three cars (Lumberjack, Jackstand 240, Coyote Mustang) plus Tom Bailey's Camaro continue to Sick Summer with the budget raised to $10,000 total; caller labels the Sick Summer videos crc2. crc1_* = Sick Week snapshot, crc2_* = Sick Summer snapshot of the same cars.

rules.fact: Original budget $7,500 (implied: Lumberjack only team under budget); $2,500 added for Sick Summer bringing total to $10,000
Engine failures from pushing the car are NOT charged; repairing with same parts is free, but upgrades (e.g. better pistons/rods) must come out of budget
Safety equipment (seats, harnesses, roll cages) not charged to budget
If you blow an engine and the replacement is no improvement, it does not go in the budget (agreed off-record)
Fair market value of used/donated parts negotiated; new rule: parts must be shown to 'the committee' before being installed
Heads-up race side bet of $500 of remaining budget (Lumberjack vs Jackstand); winner gains $500 budget

event.name: Sick Week drag-and-drive (completed); next event Sick Summer (auto-caption 'six summer') a few months later

context.name_notes: Auto-captions render Jackstand as 'jackon'/'Jackson'; he is addressed as James. 'George' appears in captions (e.g. 'georgiz Motors broke') for a Lumberjack team member - possibly Cleetus (Garrett); low confidence.

power_adder.type: single turbo (budget Amazon turbo kit, much of it carried over from team's earlier Ranger build) + nitrous

failures.cause: suspected piston/ring damage on the last cylinder (possible melted piston edge), oil burning; no definitive cause found in teardown

plans.notes: Rebuild transmission themselves, make trans-brake work, bigger injectors, better fuel system; trade nitrous for an intercooler
